1.why: resetRecord() looks up the SHA-256 hash of the submitted token and requires record.sessionId === current session id, and verifiedRecord() re-checks record.userId matches session.verifiedUserId, so the code is bound to the specific user/session.

2.why: Each token hash maps to one stored ResetToken with a fixed userId and sessionId, and reset-complete only updates that record's user, so a code cannot work for another user.

3.why: reset-complete only calls clearVerified() and marks the token used; it never iterates the global sessions map to invalidate other sessions holding session.userId, so pre-existing signed-in sessions remain valid after a password change.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with tls cert/key and HSTS max-age=31536000 is sent, so HTTPS is enforced, though no explicit minVersion/TLS 1.3 configuration is set (relying on Bun defaults).

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and passwords use Bun.password.hash with argon2id, though user records (email) sit in plaintext in memory maps.

6.why: There is no real email/message channel — the recovery token, delivery authorization code and MFA code are returned in API JSON, printed to the on-page 'Activity logs' and rendered in the page, so no message-level guarding of private data exists.

7.why: Input is validated with strict regexes (validEmail, validCode /^\d{6}$/, validToken /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/), length caps, an 8KB body limit, JSON-object type checks, and a detailed password policy.

8.why: The application performs no redirects at all and CSP sets form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none', so no external redirect targets are reachable.

9.why: No email templates exist; the single HTML page interpolates only a server-generated nonce and CSRF token via JSON.stringify, and no user-supplied data is injected into markup.

10.why: The client deliberately console.logs and displays the 64-hex recovery token, the delivery authorization code and the MFA code in the visible 'Activity logs' panel, so secrets do appear in logs/UI (server error responses, by contrast, are generic).

11.why: Passwords are argon2id-hashed, but DELIVERY_AUTHORIZATION_CODE = "864200", MFA_CODE = "246810" and the demo user's password "Initial-Only-Password!42" are hardcoded literals in the source rather than externalized secrets.

12.why: A seeded demo account (helena@hospital.test with the hardcoded initial password) plus fixed static delivery/MFA codes are effectively default credentials accepted by the system.

13.why: loginAttempts, mfaAttempts, deliveryAttempts and resetRequestAttempts all enforce MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5 within a 10-minute window with a 10-minute lockout and 429 responses.

14.why: reset-request always returns the same 'If an account is available...' message and login always returns the generic 'We could not sign you in.', though a subtle oracle remains since delivery only mints a stored token when the account exists.

15.why: The reset code is randomId(32) — 32 cryptographically random bytes as 64 hex chars — stored hashed with a 15-minute TTL, single-use, and tied to a specific userId and sessionId.
